about: What the build makes each piece of an electrical run from (Q6157 mepatoms): stock lengths, supports, boxes and their volumes, conductor colours. Values are the code's (with the section) or the trade's usual stock (marked so); a project's own documents win where they say otherwise.

EMT.strap_source: NEC 358.30(A): within 3 ft of each box or termination and at most every 10 ft
EMT.field_bend_source: the trade bends EMT 1 in and smaller with a hand bender (company default; NEC 358.24: bends made without damage)
EMT.max_bends_source: NEC 358.26: no more than 360° of bends between pull points

RMC.strap_source: NEC 344.30(A),(B)(1): within 3 ft of each box and at most every 10 ft
RMC.field_bend_source: the trade bends RMC 1 in and smaller with a hand bender (company default; NEC 344.24)
RMC.max_bends_source: NEC 344.26: no more than 360° of bends between pull points

IMC.strap_source: NEC 342.30(A),(B)(1): within 3 ft of each box and at most every 10 ft
IMC.field_bend_source: the trade bends IMC 1 in and smaller with a hand bender (company default; NEC 342.24)
IMC.max_bends_source: NEC 342.26: no more than 360° of bends between pull points

ENT.stock_source: trade stock: 1/2-1 in ENT on coils, 100 ft and up (UL 1653)
ENT.strap_source: NEC 362.30(A): within 3 ft of each box or termination and at most every 3 ft
ENT.no_locknut_source: an ENT connector snaps into its knockout (UL 1653 fittings): no locknut
ENT.field_bend_source: ENT is pliable: it bends by hand without a fitting (NEC 362.24)
ENT.max_bends_source: NEC 362.26: no more than 360° of bends between pull points

FMC.stock_source: trade stock: 1/2-1 in FMC on coils of 100 ft (UL 1)
FMC.strap_source: NEC 348.30(A): within 12 in of each box and at most every 4-1/2 ft
FMC.field_bend_source: flexible conduit bends by hand without a fitting (NEC 348.24)
FMC.max_bends_source: NEC 348.26: no more than 360° of bends between pull points

PVC.field_bend_source: PVC turns on factory elbows (company default)
PVC.max_bends_source: NEC 352.26: no more than 360° of bends between pull points

NM.strap_source: NEC 334.30: within 12 in of each box and at most every 4-1/2 ft

MC.strap_source: NEC 330.30(B): within 12 in of each box and at most every 6 ft

AC.strap_source: NEC 320.30(B): within 12 in of each box and at most every 4-1/2 ft

SER.strap_source: NEC 338.10(B)(4)(a) to 334.30: within 12 in of each box and at most every 4-1/2 ft

sq4-1.5.source: NEC Table 314.16(A): 4 x 1-1/2 square, 21.0 cu in

sq4-2.125.source: NEC Table 314.16(A): 4 x 2-1/8 square, 30.3 cu in

sq411-2.125.source: NEC Table 314.16(A): 4-11/16 x 2-1/8 square, 42.0 cu in

gang3-steel.source: NEC 314.16(A)(1): three 3 x 2 x 2-1/2 device boxes ganged, 12.5 cu in each (Table 314.16(A)); trade stock: a 3 gang steel box

gang4-steel.source: NEC 314.16(A)(1): four 3 x 2 x 2-1/2 device boxes ganged, 12.5 cu in each (Table 314.16(A)); trade stock: a 4 gang steel box

oct4-1.5.source: NEC Table 314.16(A): 4 x 1-1/2 octagon, 15.5 cu in

oct4-2.125.source: NEC Table 314.16(A): 4 x 2-1/8 octagon, 21.5 cu in

dev1-3.5.source: NEC Table 314.16(A): 3 x 2 x 3-1/2 device box, 18.0 cu in

nm1-18.source: NEC 314.16(A)(2): the volume marked on a nonmetallic box (trade stock: 18 cu in)

nm2-32.source: NEC 314.16(A)(2): the volume marked on a nonmetallic box (trade stock: 2 gang, 32 cu in)

nm3-53.source: NEC 314.16(A)(2): the volume marked on a nonmetallic box (trade stock: 3 gang, 53 cu in)

nm4-68.source: NEC 314.16(A)(2): the volume marked on a nonmetallic box (trade stock: 4 gang, 68 cu in)

fan4-2.125.source: NEC 314.27(C): a box listed for fan support; Table 314.16(A) 4 x 2-1/8 octagon

floor.source: NEC 314.27(B): a box listed for floor installation

junction.source: NEC Table 314.16(A): 4 x 2-1/8 square, 30.3 cu in (a junction where three or more runs meet)

equipment connection.source: equipment is connected in its own wiring compartment or terminal box, listed with it (UL 507 fans, UL 484 room air conditioners, UL 1995 HVAC equipment): its raceway or cable lands there, no outlet box of ours (company default; a junction box the plan shows is its own element)

box_source: the trade's usual box for the device by the wiring method (company default): on raceway the 4 in square everywhere (4 x 2-1/8 with a 1 gang ring at a wall device, with a 4 in round ring at a luminaire, 4 x 1-1/2 at a device of no known kind); on cable a 1 gang box at a wall device and a 4 in octagon at a luminaire
no_circuit_source: a device of no known kind that no circuit feeds is not known to be wired: no box until a person says what it is (its symbol is a review question)

gang.source: devices of one kind side by side on one wall face, at one mounting height, within 2 ft of each other (a plan symbol is about that wide at 1/8 in scale: symbols drawn together are ganged) share one box and one ring, up to 4 gangs: 2 gangs in a 4 in square with a 2 gang ring, 3 and 4 in a gang box (company default; power and low voltage never share one: NEC 800.133(A))

ring.source: the trade's usual ring: 1 gang, 1/2 in raised (the wall's board on the box face decides it)

default_raceway_source: branch circuits in EMT where the documents name no wiring method (company default)
insulation_source: THHN/THWN-2 copper where the specifications name no other (company default)
makeup_source: each conductor's makeup at each box: NEC 300.14's 6 in of free conductor (3 in of it past the opening of a box under 8 in) plus a 12 in field allowance for stripping, splicing and the trim cut off (company default; a project rule overrides) = 1.5 ft
panel_makeup_source: each conductor at a panel: from its entry down the gutter to its breaker, on average half the can's height (NEC 312.6 bending space), plus a box's makeup at the termination; 3 ft where the panel's height isn't known (company default)
stub_bushing_source: NEC 300.4(G) and the usual communications pathway specification: an empty raceway's stub that ends in no box or enclosure ends in an insulated bushing that protects the cable pulled in later
bushing_source: NEC 300.4(G): an insulating bushing where #4 or larger conductors enter a box or enclosure
locknut_source: one locknut per connector at a knockout (the connector's listing)
default_voltage_source: 120/208 V 3 phase 4 wire where the panel schedule gives no voltage (company default)
colors_source: NEC 200.6 (neutral white or gray), 250.119 (ground green); phase colours: the trade's usual code (company default; NEC 210.5(C) asks the code be posted)
phase_source: panel circuit numbering: circuits 1-2 on phase A, 3-4 on B, 5-6 on C (standard panelboard bussing)
feeder_makeup_source: 3 ft of each feeder conductor at each gear it lands on: from where its raceway enters, through the gutter's bending space to the lug (company default; NEC 312.6)
feeder_conductors_source: a feeder's conductors of the material its schedule names: copper THHN/THWN-2, aluminum XHHW-2 with an insulated aluminum ground, where the specifications name no other (company default; NEC 310.104)

rules.source: the luminaire's own junction box or wiring compartment, listed with it (UL 1598): fed straight, no outlet box
a canless (wafer) luminaire ships with its remote driver / junction box: no outlet box
its cut sheet mounts it on an outlet (junction) box: one box (NEC 314.27(A))
a recessed luminaire's housing carries its own junction box (UL 1598): fed by a whip or straight, no outlet box
a surface, wall or pendant luminaire hangs on an outlet box (NEC 314.27(A))

luminaire_box.default_source: the trade's usual 4 in octagon at a luminaire where neither its schedule nor its submittal says how it mounts (company default)
